newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Snake plunges Philippine city into darkness.
newsitem.headline: Snake plunges Philippine city into darkness.

text.p: Startled residents of Iligan feared Moslem rebels had resumed hostilities when an explosion rocked the southern Philippine city and plunged it into darkness.
But the culprit was a six-foot snake, National Power Corp (NPC) regional manager Basilio Iglupas Jr said on Wednesday.

The snake slithered into an NPC installation on Monday night and was electrocuted by a high-tension wire, triggering an explosion in a circuit breaker and a two-hour power cut in the mainly Christian city of 300,000 people.
"There was a defeaning explosion followed by what looked like a fireworks display lasting four minutes," said Noli Nusog, who lives near the NPC facility.
The snake was still attached to the wire when workers went to investigate.
Iligan has suffered several power cuts in recent years after Moslem rebels toppled pylons near the city.
The government and the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front signed a peace pact in Manila on Monday, formally ending 24 years of bloody conflict in the southern islands.
